biography: Ross Gunn, a name now synonymous with raw speed and relentless ambition, hails from the unassuming town of Brackley, England. His journey into motorsport began not in a karting paddock, but in the muddy fields surrounding his family's farm. Gunn's father, a weekend rally enthusiast, instilled in him a love for driving early on, letting young Ross wrestle the wheel of an old Land Rover across the uneven terrain. This unconventional training ground forged a unique car control and an instinctive understanding of grip. His formal racing career ignited with a local Formula Ford championship, where his aggressive driving style quickly earned him both wins and detractors. A defining moment came at the 2015 Spa 24 Hours, when, driving for a small privateer team, he put in a heroic stint in treacherous conditions, showcasing his exceptional wet-weather ability. Today, Gunn is a key figure within the Almond Green and Aston Martin racing programs, consistently challenging for podiums and cementing his place as one of Britain's most exciting talents. He’s known for his determination and raw speed, pushing his car and himself to the absolute limit.
drivingStyle: Gunn's driving style is characterized by an unapologetic aggression. He's known for his late braking maneuvers and a willingness to exploit every inch of the track. While some criticize his borderline reckless approach, particularly in the early stages of a race, his tire management has improved significantly over the years. He's a master of overdriving a car to compensate for its shortcomings, often extracting performance others simply can't find. Under pressure, Gunn thrives, relishing the challenge of wheel-to-wheel combat. He excels in changeable conditions, using his innate feel for grip to his advantage.

rivalries.reason: Rossi, a calculating Italian driver, represents the antithesis of Gunn's aggressive style, leading to constant clashes on and off the track.
Tanaka, a young Japanese prodigy, frequently battles Gunn for the same opportunities within the Aston Martin program, creating a fierce and competitive dynamic.
Dubois and Gunn have a long-standing rivalry dating back to their junior formula days, fueled by a series of controversial on-track incidents and a mutual respect.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky wristband, a gift from his grandmother.
Listens to heavy metal music at full volume in the garage before every race.
Refuses to have his car washed, believing dirt adds character and grip.
famousQuote: "You only get one shot at this life, so you might as well floor it."
careerHighlight: Winning the 24 Hours of Le Mans in the GTE Pro class in 2022, battling through torrential rain and mechanical issues to secure a hard-fought victory.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead on the final lap of the 2019 Spa 24 Hours, costing his team a certain victory and leaving him devastated.
